subject: Re: Model fit evals — tool/function calling & structured-output follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Model fit & tool-calling evals — next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the context on the document extraction and task-routing use cases. Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

- Key needs you mentioned: high JSON-schema compliance for extracted fields, deterministic retries for tool calls when external services time out, and a low-per-token cost for batch processing 50–100K docs/month.
- Recommended model family: Redwood LLM-3-medium-q8 with structured-output calibration. It hits the latency/throughput sweet spot on dedicated c5-like GPUs and supports our function-calling hooks for deterministic retries.
- Deliverables I’ll share by EOD tomorrow: a short benchmark CSV of our evals on a 100-doc prompt set, the prompt set (jsonl), and an example JSON Schema we recommend for your extractor.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send the benchmark + prompt set and example schema (cc: Rishi for engineering notes) — target: 4/28 EOD.
2) If those look good, we can schedule a 30-min tech sync (Rishi + Aditya) to talk about retry semantics and how we map function calls to your downstream API (recommended slot: 4/29 10:00–10:30 PDT).
3) If you want, we can spin a short POC (2 weeks) on Redwood Dedicated with sample traffic; I’ll include estimated throughput/cost in the benchmark file.

Attachments: Avery eval benchmark (stub), prompt_set_v1.jsonl, example_structured_schema.json.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.
—

From: Emma Park <emma@averyanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & tool-calling evals — next steps

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. Couple of clarifying Qs before you send the files: 

1) For JSON schema compliance: our product requires that the "amount" field is always a number and that the "vendor" field is normalized to one of ~200 canonical names. Does the example schema include normalization rules or should we push that into a post-processing step?

2) For retries: if the function call to our downstream accounting API returns a 502 vs a 5xx, do you recommend idempotent retry with exponential backoff or a fail-open with audit trail? We’re sensitive to duplicate payments.

3) On model variants: curious what regression risk looks like if we move from LLM-3-medium-q8 to LLM-3-small-q4 for cost savings. Any quick numbers you can include in the benchmark CSV?

We’re keen to do the tech sync on Thursday morning if Rishi/Aditya are available.

—
Emma Park
Head of Product, Avery Analytics
emma@averyanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & tool-calling evals — next steps

Great questions — answered inline below and attaching the benchmark + prompt set as promised. See attached CSV for per-model precision/recall on the 100-doc prompt set and an additional column with schema-violation counts.

1) Normalization: the example_structured_schema.json includes recommended canonical mapping for "vendor" for the top 50 names we see in your data and a suggested post-processing layer for the remaining ones (simple lookup + fuzzy match). For strict enforcement ("amount" must be numeric), we instrument schema validation as a hard check in the pipeline; rows failing validation can be sent to an exception queue for human review.

2) Retries & idempotency: for 502 gateway errors we recommend idempotent retry with an exponential backoff and a max of 3 retries — but only if the downstream call includes an idempotency key (we add this on the function-calling wrapper). For 5xx server errors, we recommend a short backoff + retry policy with circuit-breaker fallback to a dead-letter queue. We included a short section in the attached notes describing how Redwood’s function-calling SDK attaches idempotency keys and logs the full call/response for audit.

3) Regression risk: see the CSV. LLM-3-small-q4 drops token cost by ~40% but shows a +6–8% delta in schema-violation rate and a small drop in vendor-normalization F1. We recommend starting the POC on LLM-3-medium-q8 with a canary to small-q4 on non-critical traffic to measure actual regression.

Tech sync: Rishi/Aditya — can you confirm availability for Thu 4/29 10:00–10:30 PDT?

Attachments: avery_eval_benchmark.csv (per-model metrics), prompt_set_v1.jsonl, example_structured_schema.json, redwood_soc2_evidence_stub.pdf

—
Marissa Cole

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & tool-calling evals — next steps

Quick technical add on before the sync: 

- JSON Schema compliance: in addition to schema validation, we recommend embedding a small post-processor that enforces type coercion rules (e.g., strip currency symbols, coerce numeric strings to floats) and flags ambiguous parses. That keeps the model prompt simpler and reduces false positives.

- Function call retries: our SDK supports a "retry_state" object persisted alongside the request in Redwood’s tracing layer. For idempotency keys we recommend hashing (user_id + original_request_timestamp + fieldset_id) so replays are deterministic. For 502s treat as retryable; for certain 5xxs treat as transient but escalate after 3 failed attempts into the DLQ. We’ll demo the SDK behavior in the tech sync and share a short snippet of the wrapper.

I’ll have a 10-min demo of the retry flow and the sample wrapper code in the call. See you Thu 10:00 PDT.

—
